enonce_markdown: Two identical smooth spheres $A$ and $B$ move on a smooth horizontal table. Immediately before they collide, $A$ has velocity $(5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $B$ is at rest. At impact the line of centres is parallel to $\mathbf i$ and the coefficient of restitution is $0.6$. The speed of $A$ immediately after impact, in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For smooth spheres the impulse acts along the line of centres only. The component of each velocity perpendicular to the line of centres is unchanged; along the line of centres use conservation of momentum and Newton's law of restitution.

### Solution

Along $\mathbf i$ (equal masses $m$), with $v_A,v_B$ the velocities after impact:

$$v_A+v_B=5,\qquad v_B-v_A=0.6(5-0)=3\ \Rightarrow\ v_B=4,\ v_A=1.$$

The $\mathbf j$-component of $A$ stays $3$, so $\mathbf v_A=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$ and

$$\text{speed of }A=\sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}}=\sqrt{10}\approx 3.16\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.$$

**Answer: b.** Option a ignores the component along the line of centres, c gives $A$ the along-line velocity $4$ that belongs to $B$, and d is the speed before impact.

enonce_markdown: A smooth sphere $A$ of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ moving with velocity $(6\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ collides with a smooth sphere $B$ of mass $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ which is at rest. At the instant of impact the line of centres is parallel to $\mathbf i$ and the coefficient of restitution is $0.5$. The speed of $B$ immediately after impact, in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Only the components along the line of centres change. Write conservation of momentum and Newton's law of restitution along that line, then solve the two equations. $B$ is at rest, so it has no velocity component perpendicular to the line of centres either before or after.

### Solution

Along $\mathbf i$, with $v_A$ and $v_B$ after impact:

$$2(6)=2v_A+v_B,\qquad v_B-v_A=0.5(6)=3.$$

Substituting $v_B=v_A+3$: $12=3v_A+3$, so $v_A=3$ and $v_B=6$. Since $B$ has no $\mathbf j$-component, its speed is $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**Answer: c.** Option a is the common velocity $4$ for $e=0$, option b treats the masses as equal, and option d is the value for $e=1$.

enonce_markdown:
A small smooth sphere of mass $0.2\ \mathrm{kg}$ strikes a fixed smooth vertical wall. Immediately before impact its velocity has a component of $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ parallel to the wall and a component of $8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ perpendicular to the wall. The coefficient of restitution between the sphere and the wall is $0.5$.

Find

(i) the speed of the sphere immediately after impact,

(ii) the angle between the path of the sphere and the wall before and after the impact,

(iii) the kinetic energy lost in the impact. *[7 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For a smooth fixed wall, the component of velocity parallel to the wall is unchanged and the component perpendicular to the wall is reversed and multiplied by $e$. Kinetic energy is $\tfrac12 mv^{2}$ using the full speed.

### Solution

**(i)** Perpendicular component after impact: $0.5\times8=4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; parallel component stays $6$.

$$\text{speed}=\sqrt{6^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{52}\approx7.21\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.$$

**(ii)** Before: $\tan\alpha=\dfrac86\Rightarrow\alpha\approx53.1^{\circ}$ to the wall. After: $\tan\beta=\dfrac46\Rightarrow\beta\approx33.7^{\circ}$ to the wall.

**(iii)** Speed before $=\sqrt{36+64}=10$, so

$$\text{KE lost}=\tfrac12(0.2)(10^{2})-\tfrac12(0.2)(52)=10-5.2=4.8\ \mathrm{J}.$$

enonce_markdown: Two smooth spheres $A$ and $B$, each of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$, collide on a smooth horizontal table. Just before impact $A$ has velocity $(4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $B$ has velocity $(-2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $A$ is on the side of $B$ with the smaller $\mathbf i$-coordinate. The line of centres is parallel to $\mathbf i$ and the coefficient of restitution is $0.5$. The magnitude of the impulse exerted by $B$ on $A$, in $\mathrm{N\,s}$, is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The impulse between smooth spheres acts along the line of centres. Its magnitude is the change of momentum of one sphere along that line, found after solving momentum conservation and Newton's law of restitution along the line.

### Solution

Along $\mathbf i$ (equal masses): $v_A+v_B=4+(-2)=2$ and $v_B-v_A=0.5(4-(-2))=3$. Hence $v_B=2.5$ and $v_A=-0.5$.

$$|I|=m\,|v_A-4|=2(4.5)=9\ \mathrm{N\,s}.$$

(Check on $B$: $2(2.5-(-2))=9$.) **Answer: b.** Option a forgets the mass, c is the value for $e=1$, and d forgets that the reduced mass is $m/2$ (it gives $m(1+e)\times6$).

enonce_markdown: A smooth sphere $P$ moving on a smooth horizontal table collides with an identical smooth sphere $Q$ which is at rest. Just before impact the direction of motion of $P$ makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the line of centres. The collision is perfectly elastic ($e=1$). Through what angle is the path of $P$ deflected by the collision?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Split the velocity of $P$ into a component along the line of centres and one perpendicular to it. Perpendicular components are unchanged. For equal masses and $e=1$, the components along the line of centres are exchanged between the spheres.

### Solution

Let $P$ have speed $u$. Along the line of centres its component is $u\cos30^{\circ}$ and perpendicular to it $u\sin30^{\circ}$. $Q$ is at rest.

With equal masses and $e=1$ the along-line components are exchanged: $P$'s along-line component becomes $0$ and $Q$ moves off with $u\cos30^{\circ}$. So $P$ keeps only $u\sin30^{\circ}=\tfrac u2$, perpendicular to the line of centres.

Its new direction is $90^{\circ}$ from the line of centres; its old direction was $30^{\circ}$ from it, so the deflection is $90^{\circ}-30^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$.

**Answer: c.** Option a is the angle with the line of centres, and d is the angle between the final velocities of $P$ and $Q$, not the deflection of $P$.

enonce_markdown:
A smooth sphere $P$ of mass $3m$ moving with speed $u$ on a smooth horizontal table collides with a smooth sphere $Q$ of mass $m$ which is at rest. Immediately before impact the direction of motion of $P$ makes an angle $\alpha$ with the line of centres, where $\cos\alpha=\tfrac45$. The coefficient of restitution between the spheres is $\tfrac12$.

(i) Calculate the speed of each sphere just after the collision, in terms of $u$.

(ii) Find the angle through which the direction of motion of $P$ is deflected.

(iii) Show that the kinetic energy lost in the impact is $12\%$ of the initial kinetic energy of $P$. *[11 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Resolve $P$'s velocity along and perpendicular to the line of centres. The perpendicular components are unchanged. Along the line of centres, solve conservation of momentum together with Newton's law of restitution. Kinetic energy uses the full speeds, so include the perpendicular components.

### Solution

Since $\cos\alpha=\tfrac45$, $\sin\alpha=\tfrac35$: $P$ has components $\tfrac45u$ along the line of centres and $\tfrac35u$ perpendicular to it.

**(i)** Along the line, with $v_P$ and $v_Q$ after impact:

$$3m\left(\tfrac45u\right)=3m\,v_P+m\,v_Q,\qquad v_Q-v_P=\tfrac12\left(\tfrac45u\right)=\tfrac25u.$$

Substituting $v_Q=v_P+\tfrac25u$: $\tfrac{12}{5}u=4v_P+\tfrac25u$, so $v_P=\tfrac12u$ and $v_Q=\tfrac9{10}u$.

$Q$ has no perpendicular component, so its speed is $\dfrac{9u}{10}$. For $P$:

$$\text{speed of }P=\sqrt{\left(\tfrac12u\right)^{2}+\left(\tfrac35u\right)^{2}}=u\sqrt{\tfrac{61}{100}}=\frac{\sqrt{61}}{10}u\approx0.781u.$$

**(ii)** Angle with the line of centres: before, $\tan\alpha=\tfrac34$ so $\alpha\approx36.9^{\circ}$; after, $\tan\beta=\dfrac{3/5}{1/2}=\tfrac65$ so $\beta\approx50.2^{\circ}$. The deflection is $\beta-\alpha\approx13.3^{\circ}$.

**(iii)** Initial KE $=\tfrac12(3m)u^{2}=1.5\,mu^{2}$. Final KE:

$$\tfrac12(3m)(0.61u^{2})+\tfrac12m(0.81u^{2})=0.915\,mu^{2}+0.405\,mu^{2}=1.32\,mu^{2}.$$

Loss $=0.18\,mu^{2}$, and $\dfrac{0.18}{1.5}=0.12=12\%$.
